newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end flat, KLM off despite Q1 result.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end flat, KLM off despite Q1 result.

text.p: Dutch shares ended barely changed on Tuesday as weaker bonds and interest rate nerves eroded early market gains.
The AEX index of leading shares ended a mere 0.24 points, or 0.02 percent, higher at 979.59. In the morning, the index had hovered around five points higher.
"It's all a bit hesitant. We move a couple up, then a couple down," one trader said.
The majority of shares ended down, with the major multinationals the only significant group to gain, largely because of the continued strengthening of the dollar.
Gist Brocades was the day's largest faller, dropping over 17 percent following a profits' warning.

The company said its 1997 earnings would be below those of 1996 as the price of penicillin on world markets had hit an "historic low" due to additional capacity mainly in China and India. The shares ended down 13.90 guilders to 66.50.
However, positive company news also proved to be no guarantee of stock market success.

KLM reported a higher than expected net profit of 190 million guilders. The earnings were down 81 million guilders from the first quarter of 1996, but the year-ago figure included a sizeable contribution from partner Northwest Airlines . Operating profit tripled to 244 million guilders as traffic revenues outstripped cost increases. However, KLM's shares ended down 40 cents at 76.00 guilders.
"The good news is already in the price of 75-80. It's only natural to see profit-taking," one trader said.

Wolters Kluwer meanwhile dropped 5.00 guilders to 278.00 after reporting figures which matched expectations. Its net profits rose 21 percent to 244 million guilders against the analyst forecast of 245 million.
"The figures were in line, but they really weren't all that exciting and the shares did jump yesterday," one trader said.
